hypothesis: After the CUDA chain's promotions move experts between the card and the RAM, a prompt chunk's layer holding an expert that left the card is computed by the host, because the host pool the chunk copies from was filled once at the warm start; making the pool the non-residents again before a chunk of 128 rows or more (page-lock the experts that left, release those that came in) makes a 512-token prompt after a short conversation much faster on a T4 holding 6605 of 10240 experts, with the decode and the 64-token prompt before it unchanged.
command: cd c && make qwen36_tier.o backend_cuda.o cuda_chain.o cu_xb.o cu_tier.o CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75 && gcc -O3 -march=native -fopenmp -pthread -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-unused-function -DCOLI_CUDA -I. ../docs/experiments/qwen36-cuda-host-pool-follow-2026-10-26/bench.c qwen36_tier.o backend_cuda.o cuda_chain.o cu_xb.o cu_tier.o -o qwen36-bench -lm -fopenmp -pthread -L/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -lcudart -lcublasLt -lcublas -lstdc++; env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/root LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib64-nvidia COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text <dir>/promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 64,512 --gen 32 --teacher --steps <steps file>

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads, 38.5 MiB L3) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.storage: Google Colab VM disk (the model downloaded to /content before the runs)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.6.122+ x86_64 (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), driver 580.82.07, gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0

config.after: a 64-token prompt and 32 teacher-forced steps in the same process

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64) and, on this T4 with the code measured, make -C c cuda-test cuda-chain-check CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, tests/test_cu_tier, tests/test_qwen36_cuda_chain and tests/test_qwen36_tier_host_pool pass. The 64-token run (its prompt before any promotion, its 32 steps with them) gives in every run of both versions the same fingerprint of every logit and token (FNV-1a ffb816333a929871) and the same teacher-forced nll. After 512 the fingerprints vary from run to run in both versions (origin/dev 2 values in 4 runs, this change 2, 0 of them origin/dev's): the tier's uploads do not wait, so where an expert runs can change from run to run. The nll over the 32 teacher-forced tokens after the 512-token prompt (one text) is 2.95784-2.95785 on origin/dev and 2.93281-2.93284 with this change, top-1 14 and 15 of the 32. origin/dev ran a layer holding an expert that had left the card whole on the host's path (moe_ex: the residents as the tier's per-token groups, the other experts on the CPU in expert_ffn.h, which rounds its input to int8, QWEN_EXPERT_ACT); this change runs that layer in the chain's frame, every expert on the card's f16 GEMMs, the non-residents from the staged copies. That probably explains the change; no run here isolates it
